steps.name: Load, QC, and filter paired count data
caveats: Do not assume sample order in counts.csv matches metadata row order — join explicitly on sample ID
Flag any subject missing a control or treated sample rather than silently dropping it
steps.question: Do the counts.csv (12000 genes x 10 samples) and metadata.csv correctly encode 5 subjects each with a control and treated sample, and which genes pass a minimal expression filter for paired DE testing?
constraints: Do not perform normalization or statistical testing in this step — QC and filtering only
acceptance_criteria: Confirms metadata.csv has exactly 10 rows with subject and condition columns, 5 unique subjects each with exactly one control and one treated sample
Confirms sample column names in counts.csv match metadata sample identifiers exactly (reorders/aligns as needed)
Applies a low-count filter (e.g., retain genes with count >=10 in at least 5 of 10 samples) and reports genes retained vs the original 12000
Outputs a cleaned counts matrix and aligned metadata table for downstream DE, plus a library-size/QC summary (total counts per sample, PCA or sample correlation to check pairing)

steps.name: Paired (subject-blocked) differential expression: treated vs control
caveats: n=5 pairs is small — interpret nominal vs FDR-significant hits cautiously and note limited power for subtle effects
Subject must be included in the design formula/block; treating samples as unpaired inflates false positives and misses the paired structure the study was designed around
If neither DESeq2 nor edgeR/limma is importable in the sandbox, report this explicitly rather than substituting an unpaired t-test as if it satisfied the paired design
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control samples within each of the 5 subjects, using a paired model that blocks on subject to control for inter-individual variability?
constraints: Use raw integer counts as input to DESeq2/edgeR (do not pre-normalize with e.g. log-CPM before feeding count-based tools)
Report full results table (all tested genes) as well as the significant subset
acceptance_criteria: Fits a paired/blocked model — DESeq2 design ~subject+condition (or edgeR/limma-voom with subject as a blocking factor if DESeq2 is not importable) — never an unpaired two-group test on 10 independent samples
Confirms probing the intended package (DESeq2 preferred; edgeR+limma as fallback) succeeded before committing to it, and reports which was actually used
Reports for every tested gene: log2 fold change (treated vs control), raw p-value, and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value (padj/FDR)
Declares significant genes at a pre-specified threshold (padj < 0.05) and reports the count of up- and down-regulated genes
Includes a diagnostic check (e.g., p-value histogram, dispersion or MA plot) confirming the paired model is well-behaved for n=5 pairs

steps.name: Pathway/GO enrichment on treatment-responsive genes
caveats: No reference gene-set store was confirmed present at planning time — the step must check at runtime and degrade gracefully (report absence) rather than assume availability
Enrichment on a short, small-n-derived gene list is exploratory; avoid overclaiming pathway-level conclusions
steps.question: Which biological pathways or GO terms are enriched among the genes that significantly respond to treatment within-subject (from the paired DE analysis)?
constraints: Use the correct human gene identifier namespace matching the gene symbols in counts.csv
acceptance_criteria: Confirms availability of a human (Homo sapiens) pathway/gene-set resource (e.g., GO, Reactome, or MSigDB Hallmark) in the environment before running; if none is found, reports this gap explicitly and skips rather than fabricating results

Runs over-representation or gene set enrichment analysis on the significant DE gene list (and/or full ranked gene list by log2FC/stat) from T1S2, restricted to genes present in the 12000-gene background as the universe
Reports enriched terms with adjusted p-values, using the DE gene set as foreground and all tested genes (post-filtering) as background
Clearly labels findings as hypothesis-generating given the small (n=5 paired) input DE gene list

plan.title: Paired control-vs-treated blood RNA-seq DE analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a bulk RNA-seq blood cohort of 5 subjects, each contributing a paired control and treated sample (12000 genes x 10 samples, raw STAR/featureCounts integer counts). The paired structure is the defining feature: each subject serves as their own control, so the correct statistical model blocks on subject to remove inter-individual variability and isolate the treatment effect, rather than treating the 10 samples as two independent groups. The plan (1) loads and QCs the counts/metadata, confirming the paired subject-condition structure and filtering low-count genes; (2) runs a paired differential expression analysis with DESeq2 using a ~subject+condition design (falling back to edgeR/limma-voom with a paired blocking factor if DESeq2 is unavailable), producing per-gene treatment-response statistics; (3) performs pathway/GO enrichment on the resulting DE gene list to characterize the biological programs responding to treatment. No survival, PK, safety, or drug-target question was asked, so no translational steps are added.
